classification.difficultyReason: Model the timber constraint, form a quadratic area function and use its axis of symmetry to find feasible dimensions giving maximum area.

content.prompt: A gardener is planning to establish a vegetable garden. The garden will have a wooden border and two wooden dividers to form three partitions as shown in the diagram. Twenty-four metres of timber is used for the border and the dividers. Let $x$ m be the length of the dividers and two of the sides of the garden, as indicated in the diagram.

spec.sourceRegion: Question 8 garden diagram to the right of parts a–b
spec.description: Unshaded rectangle with two full-height internal dividers forming three side-by-side partitions. The right outer side is labelled x m. Ordinary source blue strokes are reconstructed in house black; drawn proportions are schematic and do not add numerical givens.
spec.mathematics: Four vertical timber segments each have length x; the two horizontal outer sides have the same unknown length.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the supplied x m label is visible; no derived horizontal length or optimum dimensions are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express the other side length of the garden in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
Let the other side length be $L$ m. The border and dividers contain four lengths of $x$ and two lengths of $L$.
$$\begin{align*}2L+4x&=24\\2L&=24-4x\\L&=12-2x\end{align*}$$
The other side length is $(12-2x)$ m.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Let $A$ m$^2$ be the area of the garden. Write an equation for the area of the garden in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
Area is length multiplied by width.
$$\begin{align*}A&=x(12-2x)\\A&=12x-2x^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: Find the length and width of the garden in order for the area to be a maximum.

answer.short:
Length $6$ m and width $3$ m.

The maximum occurs on the axis of symmetry of the downward-opening area parabola.
answer.worked:
For a garden with positive side lengths, $0<x<6$. The area function $A=x(12-2x)$ is a downward-opening parabola, with zeros at $x=0$ and $x=6$. Its maximum occurs on its axis of symmetry:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{0+6}{2}\\x&=3\end{align*}$$
The other side length is
$$\begin{align*}L&=12-2(3)\\L&=6\end{align*}$$
Thus the garden has length $6$ m and width $3$ m.
